messages.subject: scatter plots, overplotting, categorical data
parts:
Compare and contrast these two graphs. FWIW, I'm applying some bicycle
fit formulas to measurements taken from an anthropometric database.

ggplot(data, aes(fitstik.st, fitstik.tt.stem, color=GENDER)) +
geom_point(size=1) + stat_smooth()

produces: http://img814.imageshack.us/f/picture10.png/

In the first graph, all the "male" points are plotted underneath the
"female" points. This seems to obscure the extent of the "male" data.
The middle of the graph is dominated by blue points rather than
appearing to be an even mix.

ggplot(data, aes(fitstik.st, fitstik.tt.stem,
color=as.numeric(GENDER))) + geom_point(size=1) + stat_smooth()

produces: http://img30.imageshack.us/f/picture7hi.png/

For the second graph, I convert the factor variable to numeric. The
data is plotted in the order it occurs in the data frame (which I
randomly shuffled). Even though the colors chosen aren't as well
contrasting, it's much easier to see the overlap between the two
distributions.

I think the behavior when plotting factored groups isn't the best. Is
there a way to obtain a graph that looks like the second graph, but
doesn't force me to workaround by using numeric data and lose all the
convenience of the factor variable?

Cheers,
Peter
